hints: Equate the curve $y = cx^2 + 3x - c$ and the line $y = 2cx + 3$ to form a quadratic equation in $x$.
Compute the discriminant $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = (3 - 2c)^2 - 4(c)(-(c + 3))$ and simplify.
Analyze the sign of the resulting quadratic expression in $c$ to determine which statement (A, B, or C) holds.
walkthrough:
Set the equation of the curve equal to the equation of the line:
$$cx^2 + 3x - c = 2cx + 3$$

Rearrange all terms to one side in standard quadratic form $Ax^2 + Bx + C = 0$:
$$cx^2 + (3 - 2c)x - (c + 3) = 0$$
where $A = c$, $B = 3 - 2c$, and $C = -(c + 3)$.

Examine the value of $\Delta$ for all real $c$:
$$\text{Since } c^2 \ge 0 \text{ for all } c \in \mathbb{R}, \quad 8c^2 + 9 \ge 9 > 0$$
Because the discriminant is strictly positive for every value of $c$, the quadratic equation always has real roots (and if $c=0$, the linear equation $3x = 3 \implies x=1$ has a solution). Hence, the line and curve intersect for all values of $c$.
$$\text{Statement B is correct.}$$
